### REQ-026: Fleet management CLI (thermoctl v2) — async core, survey & inventory, OTA flash

- **Status:** DONE
- **Added:** 2026-07-04
- **Completed:** 2026-07-04
- **Verified by:** 63 pytest unit tests + live validation against the
  Bramersberg fleet 2026-07-04 (survey found 10 devices / 2 online on
  firmware 0.6.4; status/get/log/export verified on 7ROBA; set-with-restore
  `currentTarget` 19→18.5→19 on `thermo/eg/eingang`; import `--dry-run`
  showed no diff after export round-trip; offline-device timeout → exit 1).
  OTA flash verified by unit tests only (fleet runs pre-OTA firmware).
- **Depends on:** REQ-011 (supersedes it)
- **Implementation plan:** [doc/plans/REQ-026-thermoctl-fleet.md](../plans/REQ-026-thermoctl-fleet.md)
- **Description:**

  Evolve the REQ-011 `thermoctl` prototype (sync paho, `tools/thermoctl/`, never
  hardware-verified) into the fleet management tool for THermo controllers on the
  local network. The tool must double as an importable **async library** so the
  Sarah/SmartClimate home-automation system (`../sarah`, asyncio + aiomqtt) can use
  the same code without a wrapper thread.

  **Scoping decisions (Peter, 2026-07-04):**
  - Discovery: passive listen on `info/#` plus active per-device probes, results
    cached in a local inventory file. No firmware broadcast command in V1.
  - Core is asyncio + `aiomqtt`; the click CLI wraps it with `asyncio.run()`.
  - OTA is fully implemented in V1: `flash` command with a built-in temporary
    HTTP server and progress streaming. (Live OTA testing deferred — deployed
    devices run old firmware.)
  - Lives in a new top-level `fleet/` directory; package/command name `thermoctl`.
  - Broker credentials in a gitignored YAML config with named profiles; a
    committed `config.example.yaml` template; env-var and flag overrides.
  - One-shot subcommands only; the REQ-011 REPL shell is dropped from scope.
  - `set` is device-centric: `thermoctl set <deviceId> k=v [--room NAME]`;
    `--room` optional when the device has exactly one room; device-level keys
    (e.g. `logLevel`) never need `--room`.

  **Location and packaging:**
  - `fleet/` in this repo: `pyproject.toml`, `thermoctl/` package, `tests/`,
    `README.md`, `config.example.yaml`.
  - Pip-installable, console-script entry point `thermoctl`, Python ≥ 3.11.
  - Dependencies: `aiomqtt>=2`, `click>=8.1`, `PyYAML>=6`, `rich>=13`.
  - Layered: `thermoctl.fleet.FleetClient` (async library, no click/rich
    imports) + `thermoctl.cli` (presentation). Sarah imports only the former.

  **Broker configuration:**
  - YAML config with named profiles (`production`, `studentdev`, `bramersberg`)
    and a `default_profile` key. Per profile: `host`, `port`, `username`,
    `password`, optional `tls` (schema slot only in V1), optional
    `inventory_path`.
  - Resolution order: `--config PATH` → `$THERMOCTL_CONFIG` → `./config.yaml` →
    `fleet/config.yaml` (relative to the package checkout) →
    `~/.config/thermoctl/config.yaml`.
  - Overrides: `THERMOCTL_HOST/PORT/USERNAME/PASSWORD` env vars, then CLI flags
    (`--profile/-P`, `--host`, `--port`, `--user`, `--password`).
  - `fleet/config.yaml` is gitignored; `fleet/config.example.yaml` is committed
    without passwords (same pattern as `espidf/main/secrets.h.template`).

  **Survey & inventory:**
  - `thermoctl survey [--duration S] [--passive]` subscribes to `info/#`,
    harvests retained LWT/status, live status/config/log traffic and `info/new`
    announcements; after an initial listen it actively probes every discovered
    deviceId with `get {"status":""}` / `get {"config":""}` (skipped with
    `--passive`). Devices that answer a probe are `online`; retained
    `connected:false` alone marks a device `offline (retained)`.
  - Old-firmware tolerance (observed live on haus.iot.lan 2026-07-04): retained
    LWT payloads are malformed JSON (`{"deviceId":"7ROBA,"connected":false}` —
    missing quote) and must be repaired/tolerated; non-THermo devices share the
    broker (binary payloads, foreign naming) and must be ignored, not crash the
    survey.
  - Results merge into a JSON inventory file (default
    `~/.local/state/thermoctl/inventory-<profile>.json`, overridable per
    profile) recording per device: deviceId, ip, mac, firmware/app version if
    available, online state, rooms with their full config, last-seen timestamps.
  - `thermoctl devices [--refresh]` renders the inventory (id, state, ip,
    rooms, last seen); `--refresh` runs a survey first. `thermoctl rooms
    [<deviceId>]` lists configured rooms with key parameters from cached
    configs.

  **Read / write:**
  - `thermoctl status <deviceId> [--room NAME]` — live status via
    `cmd/<id>/get {"status":""}` (room-object status when `--room`).
  - `thermoctl get <deviceId> [--level user|admin|install] [--room NAME]` —
    live config; `--room` filters the printed output to one room.
  - `thermoctl set <deviceId> key=value [key=value ...] [--room NAME]` —
    builds the merge payload for `cmd/<id>/set`: room-level keys are wrapped
    in `{"rooms":[{"name":<room>, ...}]}`, device-level keys go top-level.
    Values are JSON-coerced (int/float/bool/list/string). Waits for the
    `info/<id>/config` acknowledgment and prints the changed values; non-zero
    exit on timeout. Room/device key classification from `doc/MQTT.md`.
  - `thermoctl export <deviceId> <file.json>` / `thermoctl import <deviceId>
    <file.json> [--diff] [--dry-run]` — raw round-trippable config backup, with
    structured diff and confirmation (carried over from REQ-011).
  - `thermoctl log <deviceId> [--level error|warn|info|debug] [--follow]` —
    stream `info/<id>/log/+`.
  - `thermoctl reboot <deviceId> [--yes]`, `thermoctl factory-reset <deviceId>
    --yes` — destructive commands require confirmation.

  **OTA flash:**
  - `thermoctl flash <deviceId> <firmware.bin> [--url URL] [--port N] [--yes]` —
    unless `--url` is given, starts a temporary HTTP server on this host
    (auto-detected source IP toward the broker), publishes
    `{"command":"ota_update","url":...}`, streams progress from
    `info/<id>/status` (`starting` → `progress N%` → `success`/`failed`),
    exits 0 on success / non-zero on failure or timeout, then stops the server.

  **Output:** human-readable rich tables/lines by default; `--json` for
  machine-readable output on `devices`, `rooms`, `status`, `get`, `survey`.
  Non-zero exit codes on timeout, broker error, or device failure.

  **Sarah integration:** `FleetClient` exposes async `survey()`,
  `get_status()`, `get_config()`, `set_values()`, `ota_update()`, and
  `watch()` (topic-filter event stream); README documents an import example
  for Sarah.

- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - [x] `fleet/` package installs via `pip install -e fleet/`; `thermoctl --help` works
  - [x] `thermoctl config init` writes a template YAML; real `config.yaml` is gitignored, `config.example.yaml` committed
  - [x] Profile selection via `--profile` / `default_profile`; env and flag overrides honored
  - [x] `thermoctl survey` discovers the Bramersberg fleet (retained + live + active probes), tolerates malformed old-firmware LWT JSON and foreign/binary payloads, and writes the inventory file
  - [x] `thermoctl devices` / `thermoctl rooms` render the cached inventory; `--refresh` re-surveys
  - [x] `thermoctl status <id>` and `thermoctl get <id> [--level]` return live data from a real device
  - [x] `thermoctl set <id> k=v --room NAME` publishes the merge payload, confirms from the config ack, and is verified live with set-and-restore (test targets stay **below 22 °C**)
  - [x] `thermoctl export` / `import --diff --dry-run` round-trip a device config
  - [x] `thermoctl log <id> --follow` streams live device logs
  - [x] `thermoctl flash` implemented end-to-end (HTTP server, command, progress state machine) and covered by unit tests; live OTA explicitly out of V1 validation
  - [x] `--json` output on survey/devices/rooms/status/get
  - [x] Unit tests (no broker required) pass: config resolution, topic matching, LWT repair, inventory merge, set-payload building, value coercion, OTA state machine
  - [x] `FleetClient` importable without click/rich side effects (library/CLI layering held)
  - [x] `fleet/README.md` documents install, config, commands, and the Sarah import example
- **Notes:**
  - Supersedes REQ-011; `tools/thermoctl/` (and `tools/thermotest/` scoping in
    REQ-012) remain in the tree until the legacy-tree-removal milestone; REQ-012
    must be re-pointed at the YAML config when it is picked up.
  - Live validation constraint (Peter): never set a target temperature ≥ 22 °C
    on the Bramersberg fleet — Sarah would fire the central heating.
  - No bulk/broadcast set in V1; scriptable via `--json` + shell loops.
  - Firmware broadcast discovery (`cmd/all/get`) is a candidate firmware
    follow-up requirement once the ESP-IDF firmware is deployed fleet-wide.
